newsitem.title: USA: Merrill Lynch to realign businesses.
newsitem.headline: Merrill Lynch to realign businesses.

text.p: Merrill Lynch & Co Inc said it is realigning businesses in an effort to enhance services to global clients and to position the firm for worldwide growth opportunities.
The new organizational structure, effective April 15, will be composed of four business sectors, Merrill said.

These include U.S. Private Client Group, International Private Client Group, Asset Management Group, and Corporate and Institutional Client Group. Previously, Merrill had been divided into two main business groups: Private Client and Corporate and Institutional Client.

"Our current structure has been highly effective...to the point that revenues and profits of our Private Client and Corporate Institutional Client groups are each higher today than those of all of Merrill Lynch in 1990," Merrill said.
It said the new structure will advance its commitment to delivering a world class standard of service to clients, exceptional returns to shareholders, and strong opportunities for employees.
Merrill said it plans to strengthen its international regional management structure to recognize growth and future opportunities in its business activities outside the U.S.

The firm said its U.S. Private Client Group will continue to be led by vice chairman John Steffens. Its International Private Client Group will be headed by executive vice president Winthrop Smith Jr.

It said Asset Managment will continue to led by executive vice president Arthur Ziekel and the Corporate and Institutional Client Group will be co-headed by Thomas Davis and E. Stanley O'Neal, who will become executive vice presidents.
